h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ה׳ Pesach — Maamar Hei

p: over which we recite the blessing
"Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us."
And this is what Rabban Gamliel said:
For even though we have no Pesach offering,
"we will render for bulls the offering of our lips,"
וְחָשַׁב כָּל אֶחָד עַל שׁוּם מָה,
and he reckoned each one "on account of what,"
to bring into the heart holiness from the mitzvos
through the intention for the sake of Heaven.
(and he reckoned there the order that is hinted; see there).
And it is plausible that Pesach,
שֶׁהוּא עַל שֵׁם שֶׁפָּסַח הַמָּקוֹם וְכוּלֵּי,
which is named for "the Omnipresent passed over," etc.,
"And afterward they shall go out, etc.,"
and this is the beginning of the rescue,
that He passed over, shielded and delivered.
And maror corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu,
And matzah corresponds to Yaakov Avinu,
for matzah means that there is in it no
which alludes to the evil inclination that leavens us
and that was the beginning of the serpent's incitement,
to bring desire and bodily pleasure into eating,
and this is "the leaven in the dough."
"What [even] the most frivolous of the frivolous
(רַשִׁ"י בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ט, כ"א, מִבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע', י"ח),
that is, he was like Adam HaRishon
before the sin, of whom it is written
because he knew nothing at all
and corresponding to him came the mitzvah of matzah.
But according to this it is difficult:
he ought to have said the order
why then did Rabban Gamliel put
True, in the verse too it is written
"And they shall eat the meat, etc.,
with matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it";
why were they not reckoned in the verse
in the order of the Avos?
maror is named for "and they embittered,"
which was in the Egyptian exile,
before the Pesach "that He passed over," etc.,
and matzah "that it did not have time," etc.;
so he ought to have put maror
But in truth, the matter of maror,
named for "and they embittered their lives" —
the intent is not the suffering they endured,
the intent is the purpose of the suffering they endured,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ אַחַר כָּךְ
that through it they later merited
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁתָּבַע יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
akin to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him, requesting
for his attribute is "the mighty one who conquers his inclination."
And he knew that they could not conquer the inclination
and through this they would be saved
from the evil inclination in the future,
so that there not be "sin drawing sin"
And this is why he requested suffering
that is, to rectify the past,
כְּדֵי לִהְיוֹת גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ לְהַבָּא.
in order to be "the mighty one who conquers his inclination" in the future.
And corresponding to this came the mitzvah of maror,
named for "and they embittered their lives,"
to go out of the kelipah of Egypt.
And this came at a later time,
after the Pesach, which was the beginning of the rescue,
אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח עַל בָּתֵּי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר,
"Who passed over the houses of the Children of Israel, etc.";
and therefore he put Pesach first.
But why did he put matzah before maror?
The mitzvah "in the evening you shall eat matzos"
was commanded on Rosh Chodesh Nisan,
וּפָסוּק וַיִּשָּׂא הָעָם אֶת בְּצֵקוֹ וְגוֹמֵר
while the verse "And the people took their dough, etc."
so how could he say matzah is
"on account of its not having time"?
But in truth the mitzvah was
"in the evening you shall eat matzos,"
immediately on the night of Pesach;
that is, from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,
שֶׁנִּגְלָה עֲלֵיהֶם מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים וּגְאָלָם,
for the King of kings revealed Himself to them and redeemed them,
and they then merited, for the moment,
that there be no "leaven in the dough"
in the heart of Israel at all.
פָּסַח ה' עַל בָּתֵּי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Hashem passed over the houses of the Children of Israel,
Israel merited, in the manner of
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמִצְוַת מַצָּה,
and through this they merited the mitzvah of matzah,
"in the evening you shall eat matzos," for the moment,
And afterward came the purpose of the bitterness,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ אַחַר כָּךְ
to be "the mighty one who conquers his inclination"
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה אַחַר כָּךְ,
and through this they later merited the Giving of the Torah,
for the evil inclination was entirely eradicated.
And this is what is said:
"With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it":
the purpose of the bitterness is
to be "the mighty one who conquers his inclination,"
so that through this they will merit
לִהְיוֹת אִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרַע מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
that the evil inclination be cleared away entirely,
which is the holiness of Yaakov Avinu,
Nevertheless, in time, matzah came first,
for immediately on the night of Pesach they merited,
from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,
to eradicate the evil inclination from the heart completely,
"In the evening you shall eat matzos."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ חָזַר יֵצֶר הָרַע לִמְקוֹמוֹ;
and afterward the evil inclination returned to its place;
for at the Splitting of the Sea it is written
"And the waters were to them a wall (chomah)," written deficient,
for there was prosecution against Israel,
as they said in the Mechilta
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז', וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:).
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זָכוּ עַל יְדֵי הַמְּרוֹרִים
And afterward, through the bitterness, they merited
to be "the mighty one who conquers his inclination,"
(מְכִילְתָּא הַשִּׁירָה ג', וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ס'.).
and as brought in the holy Zohar
Nevertheless, the bitterness was of benefit,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
for through it they merited the Giving of the Torah,
as they said in the Gemara
And this was the purpose of the bitterness;
and this is what is said:
"With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it."
Nevertheless, in the order of time,
they merited matzah, the holiness of Yaakov Avinu,
מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ, תֵּיכֶף בְּלֵיל רִאשׁוֹן,
from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, immediately on the first night,
"In the evening you shall eat matzos."
freedom from the Angel of Death,
for they would not have died
and as a matter of course the evil inclination would be eradicated,
for he is the Angel of Death
And therefore Chag HaPesach is called
"the great and awesome day of Hashem,"
the attributes of Avraham and Yaakov:
for immediately they merited the rescue,
from the holiness of Avraham Avinu,
and they merited "in the evening you shall eat matzos,"
the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, "the awesome"

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Gevuros Hashem 60 — “Pesach, matzah and maror make known that Israel went out of Egypt in the merit of the forefathers. The Pesach corresponds to Yaakov, the chosen of the forefathers, and so the Pesach was ‘a perfect lamb,’ for Yaakov is called a lamb: ‘Israel is a scattered lamb.’ Maror corresponds to Yitzchak, who lived in bitterness when his eyes grew dim, as the Midrash says: ‘Yitzchak initiated suffering… the Holy One, blessed is He, said to him: You have asked for a good thing, and with you I will begin.’ Matzah corresponds to Avraham, because matzah is separated from leaven; the nations have leaven in them and easily return to their bad ways, and Avraham was separated from the leaven of the nations as matzah is separated from leaven.” Connection: Maharal also pairs the three mitzvos with the forefathers and ties maror to Yitzchak through the same Midrash; he assigns the Pesach to Yaakov and the matzah to Avraham, as the forefathers' merit behind the redemption.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 65:9 — "Yitzchak requested suffering. He said before Him: Master of all worlds, if a person dies without suffering, the attribute of justice is stretched out against him; if You bring suffering upon him, it is not stretched out against him. The Holy One said: By your life, you have asked for a good thing, and with you I begin." Maror, bitterness, is Yitzchak's portion.

paragraphs.text: Rashi, Bereishis 29:21 — Yaakov said "that I may come to her": "Would not even the most frivolous of the frivolous refrain from saying so? Rather, he said it in order to beget offspring" — he was eighty-four and had yet to raise up twelve tribes. Source: Bereishis Rabbah 70:18: "Even a dissolute man does not speak in such language."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Night of Pesach 38 — “‘With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it’ was said before they left Egypt; so what is the reason ‘because the dough of our fathers did not have time to leaven’? The light of the Pesach offering shows that Israel arose first in thought even before their service, and they were commanded about matzah to show the bond Israel have with Hashem even before the completeness of their refinements. And ‘because it did not have time’ is because the body of Israel is by nature quick and eager, as was later revealed when they put ‘we will do’ before ‘we will hear’; this quickness proves they are very close to the root.” Connection: The same question of how matzah can be “because it did not have time” when it was commanded beforehand; Sod Yesharim answers with Israel's nearness to the root before any refinement.

p: And the three matzos that we take
as we have said several times
"Three — I know: three are the Avos";
And the Sages instituted four cups
corresponding to the four expressions of redemption:
"And I will take out," "and I will rescue,"
"and I will redeem," "and I will take"
And I saw a certain holy Rav who asked:
לָמָּה לֹא תִּיקְּנוּ אַרְבַּע מַצּוֹת גַּם כֵּן?
Why did they not also institute four matzos?
And in truth it would be more fitting to institute
[something] corresponding to the four expressions with matzah,
which is a positive commandment of the Torah,
and are only alluded to in "Pharaoh's cup" and the like.
But the matter of the four expressions is:
"And I will take out" corresponds to Avraham Avinu,
and it is the beginning of the Exodus,
and corresponding to it is the mitzvah of the Pesach,
וְהִצַּלְתִּי, עַל שֵׁם וַיְנַצְּלוּ אֶת מִצְרָיִם,
"And I will rescue" — named for "and they emptied Egypt,"
"they made it like a deep with no fish,"
like a fetus in its mother's womb,
for then the souls of Israel were mixed
among the souls of the nations of the world,
of the forty-nine gates of impurity.
וְזֶהוּ נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this corresponds to the holiness of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him:
to be a tzaddik who conquers his inclination.
and corresponding to it is the mitzvah of maror.
the evil inclination could still enter.
And about this is said "and I will redeem,"
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponding to the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
to be without an evil inclination,
"In the evening you shall eat matzos";
that in the end all of Israel will be clarified,
and "no one banished will be cast away from Him."
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן
prosecutions at the Splitting of the Sea,
and after that, until the Giving of the Torah,
for they would not have died,
and the evil inclination was nullified,
And corresponding to this it is said:
"And I will take you to Me for a people,
and I will be your God."
But the first Tablets were broken.
Yet we have already said that we say on Shavuos
"the time of the giving of our Torah":
even though the Tablets were broken,
one can nevertheless merit on Shavuos
the holiness of the first Tablets,
And likewise we say on Pesach
even though "we are still servants of Achashverosh,"
And afterward, with the second Tablets, they merited
that they contained Midrash, halachos and aggados,
And this is the "abundance of wisdom"
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah," etc.
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
and drink of the wine I have mixed":
the bread of the Written Torah
and the wine of the Oral Torah.
the bread of the Written Torah,
"And I will take out," "and I will rescue," "and I will redeem,"
the holiness of the three Avos.
For even though with the statement "I am"
the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts,
and with the statement "You shall not have"
the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts
the evil inclination returned to its place.
And the statement "And I will take you to Me for a people"
will be fulfilled only in the future,
when He will slaughter the evil inclination
and evil will be eradicated entirely,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבְעַל פֶּה:
which correspond to "the wine of the Oral Torah":
לִהְיוֹת אִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרַע מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
that the evil inclination be cleared away entirely,
and to merit the Giving of the Torah
as in the statement "And I will take you to Me for a people
and I will be your God,"
and the fourth cup corresponds to the kingdom of Edom,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יִזְכּוּ
for through the Oral Torah they will merit
and to merit the coming of Mashiach,
that Hashem, may He be blessed, slaughter the evil inclination,
with the coming of the redeemer,

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבְעַל פֶּה:

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 9 — “And corresponding to this are the cups that the Sages added in the Oral Torah: from the Torah there are only mitzvos of eating, and the Sages added drinking and wine, in which desire is strongest. This is the reason for four cups on Pesach night, for with Israel it is the reverse: ‘wine and fragrance make me wise.’ Through this they merit the lower wisdom, for they do not drink for desire at all but to gladden the soul for the service of Hashem, and through this speech is purified in the telling of the Exodus.” Connection: The same reading of the cups as the Sages' Oral Torah addition set against the Torah's eating mitzvos; it adds that Israel turn wine, a root of desire, into the lower wisdom of the Oral Torah.
